days.title: Programming Basics
objectives: Differentiate an algorithm and a program.
tasks: Write an algorithm to add two numbers.
Write an algorithm to calculate the area of a rectangle.
Identify the input, process and output for a student marks calculator.
Write step-by-step instructions for preparing a simple bill.
Explain the difference between an algorithm and a program with examples.

days.title: Python Environment
objectives: Set up the Python development environment.
tasks: Install Python and verify the version.
Install VS Code and the Python extension.
Create a folder named Python_Practice.
Create and execute a file named hello.py.
Run a Python program using the terminal.

days.title: Python Basics
tasks: Print your name, age, qualification and location.
Display a student profile using multiple print() statements.
Write a program using single and double quotes.
Display text on separate lines using escape characters.
Write a program to perform addition, subtraction, multiplication and division.

days.title: Variables and Data Types
tasks: Create variables for student name, age, course and marks.
Create variables using integer, float, string and boolean values.
Display the data type of five different variables.
Update the value of an existing variable and display it.
Identify and correct invalid variable names in a given program.

days.title: Input and Output
objectives: Convert input into the required data type.
tasks: Get the user's name and age and display them.
Create a program to add two numbers entered by the user.
Create an age calculator using the birth year.
Calculate the total bill using item price and quantity.
Generate a formatted student report containing name, marks and percentage.

days.title: Operators
tasks: Calculate the area and perimeter of a rectangle.
Calculate the average of five subject marks.
Check whether a number is even or odd using the modulo operator.
Calculate quotient and remainder for two numbers.
Evaluate expressions involving multiple operators and explain the result.

days.title: Advanced Operators
objectives: Check whether a value exists in a collection.
tasks: Check whether a person is eligible for a job using age and qualification.
Check whether a number is between 10 and 100.
Check whether a character exists in a given string.
Check whether an item exists in a shopping list.
Demonstrate the difference between == and is with suitable examples.

days.title: Conditional Statements
tasks: Check whether a number is positive, negative or zero.
Check whether a person is eligible to vote.
Create a student grade calculator.
Find the largest among three numbers.
Create a simple electricity bill calculator using conditional statements.

days.title: Input Validation
tasks: Create a login validation program using a sample username and password.
Validate whether an entered age is within an acceptable range.
Create a program to validate student marks between 0 and 100.
Calculate shipping charges based on purchase amount.
Create an electricity bill calculator using different consumption slabs.

days.title: Conditional Assessment
topics: Revision of variables and data types
objectives: Apply conditional statements to practical problems.
Trace the execution of a program.
tasks: Write a program to check whether a year is a leap year.
Create a calculator using conditional statements.
Create a ticket pricing program based on age.
Debug three programs containing conditional errors.
Complete a practical assessment with five conditional programming problems.

days.title: For Loop
tasks: Print numbers from 1 to 50 using a for loop.
Print all even numbers between 1 and 100.
Print the multiplication table of a given number.
Calculate the sum of numbers from 1 to N.
Print numbers in reverse order using range().

days.title: While Loop
tasks: Print numbers from 1 to 20 using a while loop.
Print even numbers between 1 and 50.
Create a countdown timer using a while loop.
Find the sum of digits of a given number.
Create a menu-driven calculator that repeats until the user exits.

days.title: Loop Control
objectives: Understand the difference between break, continue and pass.
tasks: Print numbers from 1 to 20 and stop when the number reaches 10 using break.
Print numbers from 1 to 20 while skipping multiples of 3 using continue.
Demonstrate the use of the pass statement.
Print a right-angle star pattern using nested loops.
Print a multiplication table from 1 to 10 using nested loops.

days.title: Number Logic
objectives: Extract individual digits from a number.
Apply loops and conditions to number logic.
tasks: Write a program to check whether a number is prime.
Write a program to calculate the factorial of a number.
Write a program to check whether a number is a palindrome.
Write a program to check whether a number is an Armstrong number.
Write a program to check whether a number is a perfect number.

days.title: Loop Assessment
objectives: Apply loops to solve practical problems.
tasks: Write a program to reverse a number.
Write a program to find the sum of digits.
Write a program to print all prime numbers within a range.
Create a program to print number and star patterns.
Debug and correct five programs containing loop errors.

days.title: Strings
tasks: Create a program to reverse a string.
Count the number of vowels in a string.
Check whether a given string is a palindrome.
Count the number of words in a sentence.
Create a username validation program using string methods.

days.title: Lists
tasks: Create a list of student names and display each name.
Add, update and remove items from a shopping list.
Find the largest and smallest numbers in a list.
Calculate the sum and average of list elements.
Create a student marks management program using lists.

days.title: Tuples and Sets
tasks: Create a tuple containing student details and access its elements.
Demonstrate tuple immutability.
Create a set of numbers and remove duplicate values.
Find the union and intersection of two sets.
Find common students registered for two different courses using sets.

days.title: Dictionaries
objectives: Add, update and delete dictionary elements.
tasks: Create a student dictionary containing name, age and marks.
Add a new key-value pair to an existing dictionary.
Update and delete dictionary values.
Create a contact book using dictionaries.
Create a word-frequency counter using a dictionary.

days.title: Collections Assessment
objectives: Differentiate lists, tuples, sets and dictionaries.
Select suitable data structures for problems.
tasks: Create a list of student marks and calculate the average.
Create a tuple to store fixed employee details.
Remove duplicate values from a list using a set.
Create a dictionary-based inventory management program.
Build a student record management program combining lists and dictionaries.

days.title: Functions
tasks: Create a function to add two numbers.
Create a function to calculate the area of a circle.
Create a function to check whether a number is even or odd.
Create a function to calculate student percentage.
Build a calculator using separate functions for arithmetic operations.

days.title: Function Arguments
tasks: Create a function using positional arguments to display student details.
Create a function using keyword arguments.
Create a function with a default country argument.
Create a bill calculator with an optional discount parameter.
Create an employee salary calculator using different argument styles.

days.title: Advanced Functions
tasks: Create a function using *args to calculate the sum of multiple numbers.
Create a function using **kwargs to display employee details.
Demonstrate local and global variables.
Write a function with a docstring explaining its purpose.
Create functions using basic type hints for parameters and return values.

days.title: Lambda and Recursion
objectives: Identify base cases and recursive calls.
tasks: Create a lambda function to add two numbers.
Create a lambda function to check whether a number is even or odd.
Sort a list of tuples based on the second element using sorted() and key.
Calculate factorial using recursion.
Calculate the sum of numbers from 1 to N using recursion.

days.title: Function Assessment
objectives: Apply functions to solve practical problems.
tasks: Create a menu-driven calculator using functions.
Create a student marks management application using functions.
Create an employee salary calculation program using separate functions.
Build a simple banking application with deposit, withdrawal and balance functions.
Build a mini library management program using functions and collections.
